questions.prompt: A model replies with a tool call. Your program runs the tool, adds the result, and asks the model again. Why must the second request contain the first request and the first reply?
options: Because the model keeps nothing between requests and reads only what it is sent
Because the tool result is too large to send on its own
Because the program must show the user every step
Because a tool call fails without the earlier token count
questions.explanation: The model has no memory of an earlier request. Everything it needs, including the question, the reply and the tool result, must arrive in the same request.

questions.prompt: In the loop, the reply contains no tool calls. What happens next?
options: The program runs the last tool again
The loop breaks, and the reply is the answer
The program sends an empty request to the model
The program starts a second loop with the same list
questions.explanation: A reply with no tool calls is the model's plain-text answer. The check finds zero calls and breaks out of the loop.

questions.prompt: The model replies with two tool calls. The program runs both and adds both results. How many turns is that?
options: Two turns, one for each tool call
Half a turn, because there is no text
One turn: the reply and the results that come with it
Three turns: the reply plus two results
questions.explanation: One turn is one assistant reply plus the tool calls and results that come with it. Two calls in one reply still make one turn.
